column1: What is an SBOM and why generate one?
column2: A machine-readable inventory of everything in an artifact (SPDX or CycloneDX). It answers "am I affected by this new CVE?" in seconds instead of days.

column1: cosign signs what - the tag or the digest?
column2: The digest. Signatures are separate OCI artifacts tagged sha256-<digest>.sig. A docker pull/push to a new registry does NOT carry them - use cosign copy or crane copy.

column1: Why is CVE severity a bad gate on its own?
column2: It ignores reachability. A critical CVE in a code path you never execute is lower risk than a medium one in your request handler.

column1: Right way to handle an unfixable transitive CVE?
column2: A documented, time-boxed, owned exception with a compensating control and an expiry date. Never disable the scanner; never block the release forever.

column1: Three rules for rolling out an admission policy?
column2: 1) Audit mode first. 2) Exclude system namespaces. 3) Know your failurePolicy - Fail + unavailable webhook blocks every API write cluster-wide.

column1: Distroless image - what problem does it solve?
column2: No shell, no package manager, no OS packages. Drastically smaller attack surface and near-zero CVE count.

column1: What are the four golden signals?
Never graph a counter directly. Why?
column2: It only increases and resets on restart, producing a meaningless sawtooth. Always use rate().
rate = per-second average over the window (use for alerting). irate = instant rate from the last two samples (spiky, debugging only). increase = total over the window.

column1: Correct way to compute p99 across instances?
column2: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(x_bucket[5m]))). Aggregate the buckets keeping `le`, THEN take the quantile. Averaging quantiles is meaningless.

column1: What causes a Prometheus cardinality explosion?
column2: High-cardinality labels like user_id or request_id. Every unique label combination is a separate time series. IDs belong in logs and traces, not metric labels.
Page on symptoms users feel (errors, latency). Diagnose with causes (CPU, memory). High CPU with normal latency is not an incident.

column1: 99.9% over 30 days is how much error budget?
What is a multi-window burn-rate alert?
column2: Page at 14.4x burn over 1h (budget gone in ~2 days); ticket at 6x over 6h. Catches fast burns without paging on noise.
Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, mean time to restore.

column1: What makes a postmortem blameless and why?
column2: It describes systems and decisions, never individual competence. Blame teaches people to hide information, which makes the next incident worse.

column1: The "where we got lucky" postmortem section - why?
column2: Luck is a finding. It means the same event could have been much worse, which is itself an action item.
Can someone tell whether users are having a bad time within five seconds? If the top row isn't error rate and p99 latency, no.
